overview: 2 Cheap Cars Group is a vertically integrated used-vehicle retailer in New Zealand, sourcing, importing, compliance-servicing and retailing predominantly Japanese-origin used cars through 10 dealerships nationwide under the '2 Cheap Cars' brand, with a Japan-based subsidiary (Car Plus K.K.) handling direct auction procurement. It holds roughly a 4% share of the NZ used-vehicle market, making it a sub-scale player relative to market leader Turners Automotive Group. The company is currently the subject of a NZ$0.80/share full takeover offer from Sena & Co Limited (the CEO's family trust vehicle, already ~76% owner), which would take it private and delist it from the NZX.

business_model.summary: 2CC buys used vehicles (predominantly Japanese-market imports, average age/mileage suited to NZ buyers) at auction in Japan through its own subsidiary Car Plus K.K., ships and compliance-certifies them in NZ, refurbishes/services them at a central Auckland hub, and retails them through a network of dealerships. Revenue is dominated by vehicle sale margin (a thin, transactional retail spread) supplemented by higher-margin finance and insurance (F&I) commission income earned on attaching third-party finance and insurance products to vehicle sales. Unit economics are structurally thin: FY26 gross margin of $17.4m on 7,239 units sold equates to roughly $2,400 of gross margin per vehicle, out of an average selling price in the low-to-mid NZ$20,000s — i.e. a high-volume, low-margin retail model where profitability is highly sensitive to volume, mix, F&I attach rates, and regulatory/carbon-credit costs per unit.

revenue_streams.name: Used vehicle sales
revenue_streams.description: Retail sale of imported Japanese used vehicles through 10 NZ dealerships; the overwhelming majority of revenue (~$81m of ~$81.7m FY26 revenue) but the lowest-margin line
revenue_streams.share_or_importance: ~99% of revenue, majority of gross margin dollars but lowest margin rate

revenue_streams.name: Finance & Insurance (F&I) commission
revenue_streams.description: Commission income from third-party finance providers and insurers on vehicle finance and insurance products sold at point of sale; finance penetration 31% and insurance penetration a record 44% in FY26 (up from 27% and 36% respectively in FY25)
revenue_streams.share_or_importance: Small revenue share but high incremental margin — the key swing factor management credits for FY26's H2 recovery

revenue_streams.name: Carbon credits / other
revenue_streams.description: Occasional recognition of Clean Car Standard carbon credits generated/carried forward (a one-off $1.7m benefit recognised in FY25 revenue); otherwise immaterial 'sundry income' (only $70k in FY26 vs $1.8m in FY25)
revenue_streams.share_or_importance: Small and volatile, tied to regulatory settings rather than a genuine repeatable revenue stream

business_model.customer_type: B2C — mass-market, budget-conscious New Zealand consumers, historically skewed toward new migrants and first/second-car buyers; retail transactional (not subscription/recurring)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% New Zealand retail revenue; procurement concentrated in Japan via Car Plus K.K. Domestic dealership footprint concentrated in Auckland (6 of 10 yards) plus Hamilton, Tauranga, Wellington/Petone, Christchurch.

main_competitors: Independent/franchise used-car dealer network across NZ
Trade Me Motors (C2C/dealer listing marketplace, also a customer-acquisition channel/cost for 2CC)
Direct Japanese-import 'grey market' dealers and one-truck operators
New-vehicle dealers selling near-new/ex-demo stock competing at the affordable end
competitive_position.market_position: Niche/mid-tier player with ~4% share of the NZ used-vehicle market (per Autofile data cited in FY26 annual report), materially smaller than Turners (NZ's largest used-vehicle buyer/seller, ~41,000 units sold in FY26 vs 2CC's 7,239 — roughly 5-6x 2CC's volume) and diversified across auto retail, finance, insurance, parts and vehicle servicing/repairs.

moat_factors.description: Owned Japan subsidiary (Car Plus K.K.) with staff physically inspecting vehicles at auction gives some quality/cost control versus dealers relying on third-party agents, and management repeatedly cites this as supporting 'superior inventory quality' and margin optimisation. However this is a capability, not a hard barrier — well-capitalised competitors (notably Turners) run similar or larger direct-sourcing operations, and international buyers (other RHD import markets) compete for the same Japanese auction stock, eroding any purchasing-cost edge.

The '2 Cheap Cars' brand has reasonable NZ consumer recognition in the budget segment and management explicitly positions it as 'well suited to a recessionary market,' but brand alone confers limited pricing power in a commoditised, price-transparent category where buyers cross-shop on Trade Me.

At ~4% market share and roughly one-sixth Turners' volume, 2CC lacks the scale to meaningfully out-negotiate larger buyers on auction pricing, shipping, compliance, or advertising/listing costs — if anything it is a price-taker relative to Turners.

Used-car buying is a low-frequency, highly price-sensitive, non-recurring transaction with essentially zero switching costs; there is no subscription, ecosystem or network effect locking in customers.

weaknesses: Sub-scale versus Turners, which has a diversified, higher-margin, faster-growing platform (finance book +27% YoY, servicing/repairs, insurance, parts) and a five-year plan to reach NZ$100m earnings by 2031
Single-product revenue concentration (used vehicle retail plus attached F&I) with no owned finance book of scale, parts business, or servicing/repairs annuity revenue to smooth cyclicality

Rising dependence on third-party listing platforms (Trade Me) for customer acquisition, a cost the company explicitly flags as escalating and is trying to reduce via direct-to-consumer digital investment
Directly exposed to a single regulatory lever (Clean Car Standard carbon credit costs) that swung FY26 NPAT by ~$1.7m on its own — a disproportionate share of a company earning only $3.2m NPAT
History of governance instability (2022 co-founder dispute, board/CEO/auditor turnover) that has only recently stabilised under an independent-majority board

competitors.name: Turners Automotive Group (NZX/ASX:TRA)
competitors.notes: NZ's largest used-vehicle buyer/seller; ~41,000 vehicles sold FY26 (vs 2CC's 7,239), revenue NZ$450m (vs 2CC's $82m), record FY26 profit (~$63m pre-tax before a one-off write-down), loan book +27% YoY to $566m, targeting $100m earnings by 2031. Diversified across Auto Retail, Finance, Insurance, Parts and Damage/Servicing & Repairs — the clear scale leader and the primary read-through comparable for industry conditions.

competitors.name: Independent used-car dealer network
competitors.notes: Large, fragmented base of small-to-mid sized independent yards across NZ; low barriers to entry keep the industry structurally competitive and price-transparent.

competitors.name: Trade Me Motors
competitors.notes: Dominant online listings marketplace used by both dealers and private sellers; functions as both a sales channel and a rising cost/competitive pressure (private-party listings compete directly with dealer stock, and platform listing fees are cited by 2CC as an escalating expense).

competitors.name: Grey-market/direct Japanese importers
competitors.notes: Numerous smaller importers and 'one-truck' operators competing for the same shrinking pool of compliant, fuel-efficient late-model Japanese used-import stock, contributing to rising auction prices.

growth_drivers: Cyclical earnings recovery as NZ interest rates ease, consumer confidence stabilises and net migration modestly recovers (StatsNZ reported a provisional net migration gain of 24,200 for the March 2026 year, up from 14,000 the prior year, though still well below 2022-23 peaks) — used/cheap vehicles are a historic first-purchase for new migrants

Revised (relaxed) Clean Car Standard carbon-credit settings from January 2026 (top per-vehicle penalty rates cut roughly 80%, credit expiry extended to Dec-2028) directly reduce a cost line that hit FY26 NPAT by ~$1.7m — tailwind already visible in the improved Q4 FY26 margins

Further F&I penetration gains — insurance penetration reached a record 44% in FY26 (from 36%) and finance 31% (from 27%); still below best-practice levels achieved by larger, more finance-integrated peers like Turners, implying further margin-accretive runway if the trend continues

Retail footprint optimisation — consolidating smaller/underperforming yards into larger-format, higher-traffic flagship sites (Sylvia Park opened Aug-2025, Petone opened Dec-2025) to lift throughput per site and lower average operating leverage
Reduced reliance on costly third-party listing platforms via investment in direct-to-consumer digital/brand channels, which could structurally lower customer acquisition costs over time

Increased local sourcing (direct purchase from the public / trade-ins) as a small but growing supplement to Japanese imports, which both diversifies supply and reduces exposure to carbon credit obligations on imports

business.description: 2CC has roughly one-sixth Turners' volume and a single core product line versus Turners' diversified, higher-growth, higher-margin platform; without scale advantages 2CC is structurally a price-taker in a commoditised market

business.risk: Customer concentration in a cyclically weak, low-loyalty segment
business.description: The core customer base (budget buyers, historically migrant-linked) has essentially zero switching cost and is highly sensitive to consumer confidence and credit conditions
Trade Me and other listing fee increases were called out as a driver of FY25 opex growth; the company's mitigation (owned digital channels) is unproven at scale

As a dealer holding $18m of used-vehicle inventory (FY26), 2CC is exposed to falling wholesale/retail used-car values, ageing stock, and the need for margin-eroding discounting to move slow stock, as seen in FY25's 'aggressive discounting across the sector'

financial.description: Inventory ($18.0m at FY26) is funded mainly through operating cash flow/equity rather than heavy floor-plan debt — reported borrowings were modest (~$0.75m total) and the company states it remains compliant with all banking covenants under its ANZ facilities ($5.0m trade finance, $1.0m flexi facility) — but any tightening of trade finance terms in a downturn would pressure liquidity given thin cash balances ($3.8m at FY26)

Vehicles are purchased in JPY at Japanese auction with a treasury policy of hedging shortly after auction; a weaker NZD versus JPY directly raises landed vehicle cost and compresses margin, though a stronger NZD (as in H1 FY26) is a tailwind

financial.risk: Thin equity base / low absolute profitability
financial.description: Total equity of only $22.2m and NPAT of $3.2m leave little buffer against a renewed downturn, cost shock, or extended weak trading period, and dividend payout consumes a large share of a modest earnings base

regulatory.risk: Clean Car Standard (CCS) carbon credit costs
regulatory.description: The single largest identified swing factor in recent results — CCS carbon credit costs reduced FY26 NPAT by approximately $1.7m and were the primary driver of FY26 gross margin compression in H1. Settings were eased from January 2026 (top penalty rates cut ~80% for 2026-2027, credit expiry extended to Dec-2028) following industry lobbying (Imported Motor Vehicle Industry Association) and a government policy review, but a comprehensive CCS review was due to report to Cabinet by June 2026 and the medium-term policy settings beyond 2027 remain uncertain. As an importer of predominantly older/higher-emission Japanese used stock relative to new-vehicle sellers, 2CC is structurally more exposed to any re-tightening than diversified peers.

regulatory.risk: Compliance and vehicle standards cost inflation
regulatory.description: The company has flip-flopped between insourced and hybrid (in-house plus outsourced) compliance/servicing models multiple times in recent years in response to volume volatility and cost pressure, indicating this remains an unresolved cost and operational risk

macro.description: Used vehicle demand is highly correlated with consumer confidence, unemployment (>5% in 2026) and household disposable income; 2CC explicitly attributes recent volume and margin weakness to 'the cost-of-living crisis' and 'subdued consumer confidence'

Management has repeatedly flagged that 'a substantial part of the business has historically been linked to immigration'; the sharp fall in net migration through 2024-2025 was a primary driver of the FY25 NPAT collapse, and while migration ticked up in the year to March 2026, departures of NZ citizens (to Australia) remain elevated, keeping net inflows well below the 2022-23 peak

Vehicle finance affordability is directly tied to interest rates; falling rates through FY26/27 are a tailwind (cited by management) but a renewed rate rise cycle would pressure both consumer demand and 2CC's own finance costs

macro.risk: International competition for Japanese auction stock
macro.description: Growing competition from other right-hand-drive import markets for late-model, fuel-efficient Japanese used vehicles is pushing up auction prices and tightening supply, a structural procurement headwind independent of NZ domestic conditions

governance_and_liquidity.description: Sena & Co (the CEO's family trust) holds ~76% of shares, leaving a free float of roughly 14-15% held by the general public; NZX trading volumes have historically been very thin, a fact the independent adviser (Simmons Corporate Finance) itself cited as a reason the listing provides little tangible benefit to the company. At a ~NZ$37m market cap this is a genuine micro-cap with corresponding volatility, wide bid/ask spreads and difficulty for investors to build or exit meaningful positions.

On 13 July 2026 Sena & Co issued a Takeovers Code notice of intent to bid $0.80/share cash for the ~24% of shares it does not already own, which the independent board committee has recommended (offer within the independent adviser's $0.71-$0.90 valuation range, midpoint $0.81). If successful this would delist 2CC from the NZX, removing the public equity investment case entirely; the NZ Shareholders' Association raised concerns about the deal concentrating control without offering minorities better liquidity, though it secured commitments from Sena (no creep provisions for three years, independent board majority maintained, consultation on director appointments) as partial mitigation.

2022 saw a co-founder dispute, and subsequent resignations including of the CEO and auditors; while the board has since been reconstituted with an independent majority and performance/communication have improved, this history underscores key-person and controlling-shareholder risk in a company this closely held.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The NZ used-vehicle import/retail market remains in a cyclical trough as of mid-2026: import volumes have been running 20-30% below 2024 levels for much of the past two years, driven by weak consumer demand and CCS-related cost/complexity. Turners' FY26 commentary confirms 'the used car market itself has recovered somewhat over the last year, but the big change has been the reduction in used imports coming into the country, largely down to government regulation with the Clean Car Standard' — i.e. supply-side tightening as much as demand-side weakness is shaping the market. Early FY27 trading commentary from both 2CC and the eased CCS settings point to a tentative recovery phase.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — used vehicle retail is a classic late-cycle consumer discretionary category, closely tracking consumer confidence, employment, credit availability and (in NZ specifically) net migration flows
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high, both directly (vehicle finance affordability drives volume and F&I income) and indirectly via consumer confidence and housing-market wealth effects
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Material NZD/JPY exposure on procurement; company operates a hedging policy but a sustained NZD depreciation versus JPY would structurally raise landed vehicle costs
key_input_costs: Japanese used-vehicle auction prices (rising due to international RHD-market competition)
Carbon credits under the Clean Car Standard

recent_developments.event: New flagship Sylvia Park dealership opened (Auckland, ~5,000sqm, 150-car capacity)
recent_developments.significance: Part of a strategy to consolidate smaller yards into larger, higher-traffic flagship sites; became a meaningful FY26 sales contributor

recent_developments.event: HY26 results: NPAT $1.01m (down from $1.67m HY25), revenue $39.77m (down from $42.01m), units down 13% to 3,604; interim gross dividend of 2.15 cps declared despite the downturn (70% of period NPAT)
recent_developments.significance: Confirmed CCS carbon credit costs (~$0.7m after-tax) as the primary driver of the earnings decline; management guided FY26 profitability to remain below FY25

recent_developments.event: New Petone (Wellington) dealership opened, absorbing Palmerston North volumes; New Lynn closed, Botany volumes absorbed into Sylvia Park, Westgate subleased
recent_developments.significance: Continued footprint rationalisation from 12 to 10 dealerships, aimed at improving network efficiency

recent_developments.event: Trading update/guidance: full-year NPAT expected to exceed $3.0 million
recent_developments.significance: First signal that H2 momentum (margins, procurement, F&I) was improving materially versus H1

recent_developments.event: NZ Government eased Clean Car Standard settings effective 1 January 2026 — top penalty rate for used vehicles cut from $33.75 to $7.50/gram CO2 for 2026-2027, credit expiry extended to Dec-2028, credit transfers between vehicle categories introduced; comprehensive policy review due to report to Cabinet by June 2026
recent_developments.significance: Directly reduced 2CC's largest identified cost headwind in Q4 FY26 and is a key plank of the FY27 recovery narrative, though longer-term settings beyond 2027 remain under review and therefore uncertain

recent_developments.event: FY26 full-year results: NPAT $3.2m (vs $3.3m FY25) on revenue $81.7m (down 0.3%), gross margin $17.4m (down 2%), EBITDA $8.1m (up 1%), 7,239 units sold (vs 7,675); record insurance penetration 44%, finance penetration 31%; final gross dividend 3.99 cps bringing total FY26 gross dividend to 6.14 cps (~9.9% yield on the $0.62 announcement-day price); cash $3.8m, equity $22.2m
recent_developments.significance: Confirmed guidance was met and that CCS costs (~$1.7m FY26 NPAT hit) were the swing factor versus an otherwise resilient underlying trading performance; management described 'encouraging' early FY27 trading

recent_developments.event: 2CC received a Takeovers Code notice from Sena & Co Limited (CEO David Sena's family trust, already holding ~75.9%) of intent to make a full takeover offer for all remaining shares at $0.80 cash per share
recent_developments.significance: Major corporate action — a 21% premium to the pre-announcement price and within the independent adviser's (Simmons Corporate Finance) $0.71-$0.90 valuation range (midpoint $0.81); independent directors have recommended the offer; if successful this will take 2CC private and delist it from the NZX, likely within Q3/Q4 CY2026

guidance.as_of: FY26 Results, 29 May 2026 (plus 13 July 2026 takeover notice)

items.target: No specific numeric FY27 guidance given; qualitative 'prudently optimistic' outlook, early FY27 trading described as 'encouraging'
items.vs_prior: n/a — first qualitative signal following FY26 beat-and-hold guidance pattern
items.notes: Management flagged FY27 will still be shaped by geopolitical events, domestic inflation, interest rates, fuel/shipping costs, and ongoing CCS regulatory settings

items.target: Continuation of ~60-70% of period NPAT payout as gross dividend (60% final, up to 70% interim as declared for HY26)
items.notes: FY26 total gross dividend 6.14 cps vs FY25's 6.03 cps, broadly stable despite lower gross margin, reflecting the payout-ratio policy rather than an absolute cps target

guidance.management_commentary: CEO David Sena: 'While the market environment remained difficult for much of the year, we saw positive momentum through the final quarter driven by improved margins, robust F&I penetration and better procurement conditions... Our vertically integrated sourcing model and disciplined operational focus continue to position the business well, despite the ongoing volatility across the automotive sector.' Chairman Michael Stiassny: 'We are running a tight ship, and while broader market conditions remain impossible to predict, the improved trading momentum coming into the new financial year is encouraging.' Note that with the 13 July 2026 takeover notice, forward guidance is now largely superseded by the pending change-of-control process; the independent board committee has recommended shareholders accept the $0.80/share offer, which is within the independent adviser's valuation range.

bull_case: Earnings appear to be troughing: FY26 NPAT was held roughly flat versus FY25 despite absorbing a ~$1.7m CCS cost headwind, with clear H2 momentum from improved procurement, margins and record F&I penetration
The January 2026 easing of Clean Car Standard settings removes the single largest identified drag on recent profitability just as it takes effect, directly supporting FY27 margins
A modest recovery in net migration (24,200 net gain in the March 2026 year, up from 14,000) and an easing interest rate cycle both support the historical demand drivers for affordable used vehicles
F&I penetration (44% insurance, 31% finance) still trails best-in-class levels, leaving further margin-accretive upside if the improving trend continues

The pending Sena & Co takeover offer at $0.80/share provides a clear, near-term cash exit at a premium (21% to pre-announcement price, within the independent adviser's $0.71-$0.90 valuation range) for remaining public shareholders, effectively putting a floor under near-term downside
bear_case: 2CC is a sub-scale, low-moat, price-taking participant in a commoditised industry against a much larger, more diversified, faster-growing listed comparable (Turners), with no durable structural advantage in sourcing, brand, or customer captivity

Regulatory single-point-of-failure risk remains: CCS settings eased only for 2026-2027 pending a Cabinet review due mid-2026, and any re-tightening would again disproportionately hit a company where a single line item moved NPAT by more than half in one year

The business remains highly cyclical and geared to two macro variables largely outside its control — NZ consumer confidence/employment and net migration — both of which remain well below pre-2023 levels even after recent stabilisation

Micro-cap NZX illiquidity, an extremely concentrated share register (~76% held by the CEO's trust), and a history of governance turbulence (2022 co-founder dispute, board/CEO/auditor turnover) make this a structurally weak minority-shareholder proposition even before the takeover

If the pending Sena & Co takeover succeeds, the public equity investment case ends entirely via delisting, and the offer price ($0.80) — while within the independent valuation range — caps upside for anyone buying above that level or hoping for a materially higher bid, given the near-90% controlling position already held by the bidder

moat_rating.justification: 2CC operates in a fundamentally commoditised, low-barrier-to-entry industry (used vehicle import and retail) where products are largely undifferentiated, price comparison is trivial via platforms like Trade Me, and customers have zero switching costs. Its vertically integrated Japan-sourcing model is a genuine operational capability that supports inventory quality and modest cost control, but it is neither unique nor scale-advantaged versus the market leader Turners, which runs a comparable or larger direct-sourcing operation alongside a materially more diversified and profitable platform. Brand recognition in the budget segment provides at most a narrow, easily-contestable edge. There are no network effects, regulatory barriers protecting incumbents, or meaningful switching costs — if anything, 2CC is a price-taker relative to larger, better-capitalised competitors, and its recent earnings volatility (driven almost entirely by a single external regulatory cost line) underscores the absence of a durable buffer against industry and policy shocks.

management_assessment: CEO David Sena is the company's founder and controlling shareholder (via Sena & Co, ~76% owner) and has led the operational turnaround since the 2022 governance crisis, with credible recent execution — footprint rationalisation, F&I penetration gains, and cost discipline through a very difficult FY25/FY26 trading environment, delivering results in line with or ahead of guidance in both years. Chairman Michael Stiassny and the reconstituted independent-majority board appear to have restored governance credibility following the 2022 turmoil (co-founder dispute, CEO/auditor resignations). However, the founder's near-total ownership concentration is a double-edged sword: it aligns incentives for operational performance but has also now culminated in a related-party takeover bid where the CEO is effectively both dominant shareholder and the person setting the terms on which minorities are bought out — a scenario the NZ Shareholders' Association flagged as concerning before securing minority-protective commitments (no creep for three years, independent board majority, consultation on director appointments) as a condition of support. Overall: capable operational management within a structurally difficult industry, but governance independence for public minority holders has always been, and remains, limited by the extreme concentration of control.

dividend_profile.policy: 2CC targets a gross dividend payout of approximately 60% of full-year NPAT (with the interim dividend historically set at up to 70% of first-half NPAT, trued up at the final dividend to bring the full-year payout to around 60%)
dividend_profile.current_yield_and_recent_history: FY26 total gross dividend was 6.14 cps (final 3.99 cps + interim 2.15 cps), up marginally from FY25's 6.03 cps, against FY24's materially higher 11.56 cps — illustrating how sharply the dividend has already been cut in line with the NPAT collapse from FY24's peak (~$6.2m NPAT, 14 cps EPS) to FY25/FY26's trough (~$3.2-3.3m NPAT, 7 cps EPS). At the $0.62 share price prevailing on the FY26 announcement date, the trailing gross yield was approximately 9.9%; at the current ~$0.795 share price (post-takeover-notice run-up) the equivalent trailing yield is closer to 7.7%.
dividend_profile.sustainability_assessment: The payout ratio policy (rather than a fixed cps target) is inherently self-adjusting to the earnings cycle, which is a sensible discipline for a cyclical micro-cap and has kept the dividend broadly stable in absolute cents even as underlying earnings roughly halved from FY24 to FY25. Balance-sheet support is reasonable: modest formal borrowings (~$0.75m), positive operating cash flow ($4.2m FY26, albeit down from $6.7m FY25), and continued covenant compliance under ANZ trade-finance facilities. However, the dividend is being paid out of a genuinely depressed and volatile earnings base (single-digit-million NPAT that swung by ~$1.7m from one regulatory cost line alone), inventory levels are rising ($18.0m FY26 vs $14.9m FY25) which consumes cash that could otherwise support distributions, and cash on hand has been trending down ($5.3m to $4.6m to $3.8m over the last three half/full-year balance dates). The high headline yield is therefore best read as compensation for cyclical/regulatory earnings risk rather than a low-risk income stream, and is now in any case likely to be superseded by the pending takeover, which would end the public dividend stream via delisting.

valuation_context.framing: 2CC should be assessed as a small-cap, cyclical, dividend-paying value/turnaround situation rather than a growth story. At a market capitalisation of roughly NZ$37m against FY26 NPAT of $3.2m, the stock trades around 11-12x trailing depressed earnings pre-takeover-notice (at the $0.62-0.75 range seen through FY26), a level that reflects both the cyclically low earnings base and a discount for micro-cap illiquidity/governance concentration. The independent adviser (Simmons Corporate Finance) engaged as part of the Sena & Co takeover valued 2CC's ordinary shares at $0.71-$0.90 per share (enterprise value $32.3m-$41m), with the offered $0.80/share sitting close to the midpoint ($0.81) — providing a rare, recent, professionally-derived valuation anchor for the stock. With the shares now trading close to the $0.80 offer price (52-week range $0.475-$0.81, current ~$0.795), the market is pricing in a high probability of the takeover completing at or near the offer terms, meaning further re-rating upside for public holders is likely capped unless a competing bid emerges (which appears unlikely given Sena & Co's ~76% blocking stake) or the independent adviser's process results in an increased price.
valuation_context.historical_multiple_context: Earnings and dividends have been highly volatile since listing (Feb-2021 IPO): NPAT/EPS peaked around FY24 (~14 cps underlying EPS) before roughly halving in FY25 (7 cps) and holding flat in FY26 (7 cps), so any P/E view must be earnings-cycle-adjusted rather than based on a single trailing year; the FY24 peak-earnings multiple would look far cheaper than the current trough-earnings multiple at the same share price, underscoring the cyclicality rather than a re-rating in intrinsic value.

investment_summary: 2 Cheap Cars Group is a sub-scale, low-moat New Zealand used-vehicle retailer whose earnings power has been squeezed over the past two years by a genuinely severe combination of macro (weak consumer confidence, a multi-year collapse and only partial recovery in net migration) and regulatory (Clean Car Standard carbon credit costs, which alone cost the company roughly $1.7m of FY26 NPAT) headwinds, on top of structural competitive disadvantages versus the much larger and more diversified market leader, Turners Automotive Group. The business has no meaningful moat in a commoditised, price-transparent industry, and its vertically integrated Japan-sourcing model — while operationally sound — is neither unique nor scale-advantaged. That said, the FY26 result showed genuine signs of a trough forming: second-half momentum from improving procurement, record F&I penetration, and eased CCS settings from January 2026 all point toward a plausible FY27 earnings recovery, and management's guidance has been met or exceeded in each of the last two years. Historically, the investment case here has rested on a high, payout-ratio-linked dividend yield (~8-10% gross at various points in FY25/26) as compensation for cyclical and regulatory earnings risk, underpinned by a reasonably conservative balance sheet (modest formal debt, covenant compliance). However, the situation has now been overtaken by a more decisive event: on 13 July 2026, CEO David Sena's ~76%-owning entity Sena & Co issued a Takeovers Code notice to acquire the remaining shares at $0.80 cash per share, a price within the independent adviser's $0.71-$0.90 valuation range and recommended by the independent board committee. With the shares trading near the offer price, the practical investment question for remaining or prospective holders is no longer primarily about the underlying auto-retail cycle but about takeover mechanics — whether to accept the cash offer, hold for a possible (but unlikely, given the bidder's blocking stake) higher bid, or exit on-market. Absent the takeover, 2CC would remain a legitimate but honestly second-tier micro-cap income/value idea: cyclical, regulation-exposed, illiquid, and closely controlled, offering a recovering but still fragile earnings base rather than a business with durable competitive advantage.
sources_note: Analysis draws on 42 extracted 2CC company documents (FY2021-FY2026 annual reports, half-year reports and announcements, results/market announcements, investor and ASM presentations, and the 2021 IPO Listing Profile) located in ./2CC.NZ/Extracted/, supplemented by web research (July 2026) on Clean Car Standard policy changes (Ministry of Transport, Beehive.govt.nz, Drive Electric, Newsroom), NZ migration data (Stats NZ), Turners Automotive Group FY26 results (Kalkine, NewsWire, TipRanks), and the Sena & Co takeover notice and related commentary (NZX announcement #475952, NBR, Autofile, BusinessDesk, NZ Shareholders' Association).
